narrative: On September 27th at approximately 10:00 am, Stripping Machine Operator reported material smoldering on the ground under the brush machine at the Stripping Station. The operator reported the Brush on the south side of the machine was vibrating due to excessive wear, so he decided to use only the brush on the North side of the machine. The excessive use of one worn brush resulted in higher friction during the stripping process, resulting in overheating the material when it 'clogged' on the brush, as it was removed from the pipe. Operator immediately shut down the operation, utilized a fire extinguisher and eliminated any potential fire. The operation remained shut down until Maintenance personnel completed the maintenance and troubleshooting on the north and south brush. There were no injuries and no damage occurred to the equipment or pipe.

narrative: On 19th December at 09:45, a truck was carrying materials from Jetty to the Kaombo storage area. The truck failed to ascend the slope coming from the Jetty, the driver tried three times but the truck didn't have capacity to ascend the slope. The truck driver contacted OPS team leader to provide an Excavator CAT 385C to provide support and pull the truck. In the process of pulling the truck, one of the Excavator Hydraulic hoses burst causing a leakage of approximately 20 liters of hydraulic oil to the ground. A lack of communication between the excavator operator and the truck driver, neither of them had radios, caused the excavator to start pulling the truck while the truck brakes were still "ON". This situation caused an overload of pressure in the excavator hydraulic system eventually leading to burst a hose.

narrative: Background:_x000D_ The Deep Orient is conducting Subsea Installation operations on the Prelude OIC2. On 08/10/2016 ROV XLX74 experienced an incident where the Forward Port Lateral Thruster Hydraulic Hose B2 ruptured during subsea operations causing loss of power to the thrusters and 3ltes of hydraulic oil to be lost to the sea (Synergi report 511732 refers). Another hose failure of the same hydraulic hose occurred on XLX 75 on 10/10/2016 (Synergi no.511956 refers). In both incidents the cause has been suspected as due to poor routing of the hydraulic hose on the vehicle which is causing the hose to rupture internally._x000D_ _x000D_ Environmental Conditions:_x000D_ Vessel maintaining position with good visibility at night, calm sea with significant wave height of 0.5m. Wind speed 4KN. Subsea visibility conditions were workable with a current of 1.7KN on the surface DP desk monitor. _x000D_ _x000D_ Task / Actions Leading up to the Incident:_x000D_ ROV XLX75 had completed disconnection of brace rigging on MJ1. The ROV was then in preparation to commence connecting tagging rigging to brace._x000D_ _x000D_ Incident/Initial findings:_x000D_ At 19:10 at depth of 50m during operations to initiate Tag lines to Spreader bar for recovery to surface, the current at the working depth had increased which was hampering ROV XLX 75 ability to maintain required position/station to conduct works. _x000D_ Whilst trying to maintain station at the worksite and keep the ROV in a safe position the ROV had to be operated at 100% joystick control and full system pressure. _x000D_ During these manoeuvres the Port Aft (Lower) Lateral Thruster Hose ruptured and failed._x000D_ At time of hose failure the works had been suspended due to an unexpected excessive current, spreader was then lowered to 100m to check conditions, current improving.._x000D_ ROV XLX75 team made preparations to return defective sub to TMS, conditions at 50m not suitable to recover ROV to TMS, lowered TMS to 170m effecting safe recovery of ROV; ROV XLX on deck 19:44_x000D_ _x000D_ It is estimated that approx. 3 litres of T32 hydraulic oil was discharged from the vehicle into the sea during the event._x000D_ _x000D_ The immediate cause of the loss of hydraulic oil has been determined as a Port Aft (Lower) Lateral Thruster Hose failure._x000D_ _x000D_ It has been identified that the hydraulic hose has failed in the same area as 2 previous incidents which has further confirmed a routing issue with the hoses._x000D_ _x000D_ The hydraulic hose used on both vehicles is a Parker 471 ST Hydraulic Hose with 2-wire braided compact construction See details below._x000D_ _x000D_ Evidence of planned maintenance and pre-dive checks have identified that there were no externally visual signs of wear, deformity or damage to the hose._x000D_ _x000D_ RIS Regional Manager TMOS/Subsea Operations APAC has been advised of all incidents.

narrative: On July 11th, 2017 at approx. 1700 the Sea Hunter light diving craft was being moored at position 4S alongside the Sea Rose FPSO. The detector FRC was assisting with the operation. The bow line had already been attached and the FRC was assisting with the connection of the 2 stern lines. The FRC crew had attached the first stern line to the FPSO festoon line and were in the process of transferring the loose end to the deck personnel on the LDC. The loose end was handed to the LDC crew on the starboard aft of the LDC then whilst the LDC crew were in the process of transferring it to the port aft bollard the FRC crew threw the excess slack into the water. The LDC deck crew came up quickly on the rope but not in time to prevent the bite getting sucked into the starboard jet drive intake._x000D_ At this point the starboard engine stalled out. The LDC crew pulled up as much of the slack rope that they could and secured it to the aft railing. The LDC crew completed disconnection of the bow line and then proceeded to returned to the Maersk Detector for recovery back onboard._x000D_ When the LDC was approx. 50M from the Detector it would appear that the tail end of the rope that was sucked into the starboard jet drive became caught in the port jet drive and was pulled clear of the starboard side. The starboard engine was restarted and was the primary means of propulsion for recovering the LDC back to the Detector.

narrative: The incident happened during stacking of stalks and preparations for spooling operations. The task was to take one stalk from rack and place it on top of the stack, second tier. The stalk they were roller boxing was approximately 700meters long (Short stalk). Everything went well until they reached the end of the stalk. When taking the roller boxes of the stalk-end they noticed that approximately 30 meters from the end, the stalk was not in the correct position (about 15meters of the stalk was in the groove next to the correct one). Operators tried to correct the position of the stalk by using a soft sling and pulling the stalk in position. When the stalk fell into the groove it had to much momentum and slide of the stalk and down to the rack, approximately 40cm down. Due to the position of the stack it was limited space between intermediate tie-in and the stack. When the stalk slide down, it hit the side wall of intermediate tie-in. There was no people in the area and there was no damage to the stalk itself. Minor constructional damage to the wall of intermediate tie-in.  _x000D_ _x000D_ Please see attached photos of damage to intermediate tie-in and internal deviation report for Mardahl Maskin AS.

narrative: Environmental Conditions: _x000D_ The event was noted at 1600 on 10/03/2019. _x000D_ The Deep Blue was in transit for Leviathan project from Mobile to Limassol. The vessel was proceeding to Algeciras on a course of 079 degrees true with speed 10 knots for crew change._x000D_ Wind was from 125 degrees true and speed 12/18 knots. Sea was from 100 degrees true with sig wave 2m_x000D_ _x000D_ Task/ actions leading up to the incident: _x000D_ During Inspection of the area, a blue green fluid was noticed on the floor plates of the Aft Carousel next to the 1st End UTA_x000D_ _x000D_ Initial findings: _x000D_ The fluid was determined to be Oceanic HW 540 P. It had not been in contact with any personnel and presented no harm. Only direct contact with the fluid to the eyes and if swallowed can be hazardous as per the SDS. _x000D_ The leakage was contained onboard, internally within the confines of the immediate area of deck in the Aft Carousel next to the 1st End UTA. _x000D_ Further investigation determined most probable cause to be leakage / weeping from the monitoring equipment set up on the 1st End UTA in the Aft Carousel._x000D_ There was no drop in pressure. The pressure report of the umbilical for the aft carousel was the same as the morning. _x000D_ _x000D_ Immediate Actions:_x000D_ Barge Engineer started investigation and Construction Crew commenced bunding / containment of the leaked fluid on the Carousel floor plates. OMT was notified._x000D_ _x000D_ Additional Information:_x000D_ While cleaning up/investigating the source of the leak, SOPEP pads were noticed in place on a bundle of hydraulic hoses. There was a significant amount of fluid resting in the area. _x000D_ It was later determined that when disconnecting from the main umbilical, Halliburton personnel had accidentally opened a manifold valve resulting to a small spillage. The valve was shut as soon as it had noticed, the spillage cleaned up and additional spill pads left as a precaution. The vessel was not informed of this at the time.
